title: LCA of Corrugated Cardboard E-commerce Packaging: Right-Sizing, Recycled Fibre and Reuse
sub: A cradle-to-grave assessment of shipping packaging for a 1 kg online order, comparing an oversized box, a right-sized box, a recycled-fibre box and reusable shipping packaging.
pdf: Case 05 — LCA of E-commerce Cardboard Packaging: Executive Summary
fu: Packaging to protect and deliver one 1 kg non-fragile e-commerce order (shoebox size) from a fulfilment centre to a household in Germany
ref: Baseline: one 450 g oversized single-wall corrugated box (50% recycled fibre) with 12 g plastic air-pillow void fill. Alternatives: 260 g right-sized box; 260 g 100% recycled box; reusable polypropylene shipper (300 g, 20 effective cycles)
boundary: Cradle-to-grave: forestry and fibre recovery, pulping and paper making, corrugating and box making, void fill, transport to the fulfilment centre, parcel delivery (allocated by volume), recycling, incineration or return logistics
geo: Containerboard and boxes produced in Germany; delivery and end-of-life in Germany
time: 2024–2026 technology; GWP100 (IPCC AR6); biogenic carbon treated as neutral
method: EF 3.1 characterisation; IPCC AR6 GWP100; AWARE for water scarcity; ReCiPe 2016 land occupation
alloc: Parcel delivery emissions allocated by parcel volume share in the van; recycled fibre via cut-off; reusable packaging burdens divided by effective number of cycles including losses
cutoff: Flows <1% of mass and energy excluded (tape, adhesive, labels) with cumulative exclusions <5%
dq: FEFCO European database for corrugated board, ecoinvent, parcel-delivery literature; no retailer data. Overall data quality Medium
srcShort: Illustrative model; parameters within ranges from the FEFCO/CEPI European database for corrugated board, ecoinvent and published e-commerce packaging LCAs.
loop: Circular loop: boxes recycled into new containerboard; reusable shippers returned via post
exec:
This case study assesses the packaging needed to deliver a 1 kg online order, a high-volume decision for every e-commerce business. Packaging for e-commerce is under scrutiny because of empty space in parcels; the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation will limit empty space ratios in grouped, transport and e-commerce packaging.
The illustrative baseline (an oversized 450 g box with plastic void fill) results in 0.62 kg CO2e per order. Parcel delivery is the largest contributor (48%), because an oversized box takes more space in the delivery van. Paper making contributes about a third.
Right-sizing the box to 260 g and removing void fill reduces the result by about 41% to 0.37 kg CO2e. Using 100% recycled fibre gives a small additional reduction (to 0.35 kg). A reusable shipper reaches 0.33 kg CO2e at 20 effective cycles, but only beats the right-sized recycled box after about 13 cycles, and depends on customers returning it.
The key recommendation is to right-size packaging first, then consider recycled fibre and reuse where return rates can be secured. For CSRD, results support ESRS E5 (packaging inflows and outflows), E1 (Scope 3 Categories 1, 4 and 9) and E4 (forest fibre sourcing).
overview:
Corrugated cardboard boxes are the default packaging for online orders. They are made from containerboard (liner and fluting) produced from virgin wood fibre, recovered paper, or both, and are among the most recycled packaging materials in Europe.
The purpose of this LCA is to show how packaging size, fibre source and reuse affect impacts, including the often-overlooked effect of packaging volume on delivery emissions.
goal: The goal is to support an online retailer's packaging design and procurement and its PPWR readiness. The audience is packaging, logistics, procurement and sustainability teams. Results are for internal use.

lci: Volume-based share of van and hub emissions

hot.why: An oversized box takes more space in delivery vans, so more trips are needed. Allocated by volume, delivery is the largest contributor (≈48%).
Drying paper is energy-intensive; mills using natural gas or grid electricity drive most of the box's own footprint and water use.
An oversized box uses about 75% more board than needed, increasing every upstream impact.
Air pillows add fossil-based material that is rarely recycled from households.

desc: 450 g box, 50% recycled fibre, 12 g LDPE air pillows
260 g box fitted to the product, no void fill; 33% less van volume
As right-sized, made from 100% recycled fibre
300 g PP shipper, 20 effective cycles (85% return rate), returned flat by post

sens.t: Sensitivity: number of effective cycles of the reusable shipper
sens.xl: Effective use cycles per reusable shipper
sens.note: The reusable option depends on how many times each shipper is actually used, which depends on return rates and damage.
sens.interp: The reusable shipper breaks even with a right-sized recycled box at about 13 cycles; below that it is worse. Beyond 50 cycles gains are small because return postage and delivery dominate.

ci.stage: Parcel delivery and paper making together account for over 80% of the baseline. Right-sizing reduces both.
ci.stage_e: Paper making dominates energy demand, including a substantial share of renewable biomass energy at virgin-fibre mills.
ci.stage_w: Water consumption occurs almost entirely at the paper mill.
ci.donut: Nearly half the result comes from delivery, which is often excluded from packaging LCAs; including it changes the priorities.
ci.sankey: About 85% of the box returns as recovered paper; plastic void fill ends up entirely in residual waste.
ci.heat: Paper making is a hotspot for climate, energy and water; parcel delivery for climate and particulates; fibre sourcing for land use.
ci.scen: Right-sizing gives the largest single reduction; recycled fibre adds little; reuse helps if cycles are high.
ci.radar: The reusable shipper performs best on water, waste and land; the right-sized recycled box is close on climate with no return-rate risk.
ci.wf: Right-sizing and the associated delivery saving are as large as electrifying delivery vans; recycled fibre is a minor lever.

interp.m: For e-commerce packaging, size matters more than material. Right-sizing reduces packaging material and delivery emissions at the same time.
interp.a: Allocation of delivery emissions by volume; number of reuse cycles and return rates; mill energy mix; recycled fibre share.
interp.u: Delivery allocation method is uncertain (volume vs weight); real return rates for reusable packaging; mill-specific energy sources.
interp.can: Right-sizing and eliminating void fill are robust improvements; reuse can help with high return rates.
interp.cannot: The study cannot show that recycled fibre always has lower climate impact (mill energy matters), or that reusable packaging works for all product types.
interp.d: Packaging-size range rationalisation, automated box-on-demand systems, fibre procurement, reuse pilots with KPI tracking, PPWR empty-space compliance.

recs: Design packaging to product dimensions and use box-on-demand machines; replace plastic void fill with paper only where fill is needed.
Specify board grades by required performance rather than default grammage; require FSC/PEFC certification for virgin fibre.
Use renewable steam and electricity at mills; maximise recycled fibre where strength allows.
Reduce box size range mismatches, consolidate orders, and pilot reusable shippers in markets with high return compliance.
Maintain high-quality paper collection; reduce contamination from tape and plastic.
Track empty-space ratio, packaging weight per order and recycled content as E5 metrics; include delivery in Scope 3 Category 9 accounting.
Enforce PPWR empty-space limits and support standardised reusable packaging pools.

take: For e-commerce, the best packaging change is a smaller box: right-sizing cuts material and delivery emissions together, by about 40% in this model.
biz: Right-size packaging across the range before switching materials, eliminate plastic void fill, and pilot reusable shippers only with tracked return rates above the break-even point.
assume: Delivery emissions allocated by parcel volume; oversized parcel uses 50% more van space; 85% box recycling; reusable shipper 20 effective cycles at 85% return rate; biogenic carbon neutral.
